GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency. 32.

Article 19

1. Parents, guardians and/or family legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
2. Parents and/or family must carry out prevention of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and prevailing norms.
3. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12

1. Other violence as referred to in Article letter constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict the fundamental freedom of a person.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 26

Forms of services to victims as referred to (1 in Article 24 letter b, are as follows:
a. services to women and children victims of acts of violence, include:
1\. complaint, consultation and counseling services;
2\. assistance services;
3\. health services;
4\. legal aid services;
5\. repatriation and social reintegration services; and
6\. social rehabilitation services.
b. in addition to the forms of services regulated in letter also provided special services which include:
1\. pick-up services; and/or
2\. medical and psychological referral services.
2. Forms of services as referred to in paragraph (1) letter and letter b, are implemented by Regional Apparatus according to minimum service standards established by the government.
3. Further provisions regarding the implementation of services (3) as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. The community has obligations and responsibilities for the protection of women and children victims of violence through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 18

The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government (1) as referred to in Article 17 letter a, include:
a. preparing and implementing programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implementing the protection of women and children;
c. supervising services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocating budget for the protection of women and children from acts of violence according to regional financial capacity.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government prepares programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
3. The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
4. Further provisions regarding the regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be further stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

This Regional Regulation is intended as:
a. fulfillment of the rights of children and women in the context of protection and prevention of violence against children and women in the Region; and
b. guidelines for Regional Government and the community to provide protection, services, medical rehabilitation, social rehabilitation and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VII

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 45

Any person who intentionally commits violence against women and children as referred to in Article up to Article 12 shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Article 7

Physical violence as referred to in Article letter constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

Article 41

1. In order to achieve the objectives of the protection of women and children as referred to in Article 4, the Regional Government may cooperate with other parties in accordance with (1) the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses.
3. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of Joint Agreement and/or Cooperation Agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 9

Sexual violence as referred to in Article letter includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Article 40

1. The Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons as referred to in Article 38 letter b, is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling (1 of trafficking in persons.
2. The Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in Article 38 letter c, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women.
3. Provisions regarding the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons and the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Paragraph General

Article 22

The Regional Government in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence through activities:
a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. b. in addition to the forms of services regulated in letter also provided special services which include:

2\. medical and psychological referral services.

Article 19

Article 7

Physical violence as referred to in Article letter constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

Article 9

Sexual violence as referred to in Article letter includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking. 34. 1. Region is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency. 32.

CHAPTER VI

FUNDING

Article 43

1. The Regional Government shall allocate budget/financing for the implementation of protection of women and children up to the village level.
2. The implementation budget as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be sourced from the Regional Budget and may be sourced from other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. The budget as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be used for prevention, service, handling, protection and empowerment activities for women and children.

Article 19

1. Parents, guardians and/or family legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
2. Parents and/or family must carry out prevention of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and prevailing norms.
3. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 34

Empowerment as referred to in Article 22 letter is carried out for women victims of violence, in the form of:
a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.

Article 24

Services as referred to in Article 22 letter b, take into account:
a. service principles; and
b. forms of services to victims.

Article 26

Forms of services to victims as referred to (1 in Article 24 letter b, are as follows:
a. services to women and children victims of acts of violence, include:
1\. complaint, consultation and counseling services;
2\. assistance services;
3\. health services;
4\. legal aid services;
5\. repatriation and social reintegration services; and
6\. social rehabilitation services.
b. in addition to the forms of services regulated in letter also provided special services which include:
1\. pick-up services; and/or
2\. medical and psychological referral services.
2. Forms of services as referred to in paragraph (1) letter and letter b, are implemented by Regional Apparatus according to minimum service standards established by the government.
3. Further provisions regarding the implementation of services (3) as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. The community has obligations and responsibilities for the protection of women and children victims of violence through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 3

This Regional Regulation is intended as:
a. fulfillment of the rights of children and women in the context of protection and prevention of violence against children and women in the Region; and
b. guidelines for Regional Government and the community to provide protection, services, medical rehabilitation, social rehabilitation and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

Article 40

1. The Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons as referred to in Article 38 letter b, is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling (1 of trafficking in persons.
2. The Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in Article 38 letter c, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women.
3. Provisions regarding the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons and the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 41

1. In order to achieve the objectives of the protection of women and children as referred to in Article 4, the Regional Government may cooperate with other parties in accordance with (1) the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses.
3. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of Joint Agreement and/or Cooperation Agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 37. Empowerment is a process of developing independence and welfare of a person or community by increasing knowledge and skills to meet their life needs both economically and socially. 38. Restorative Justice is the settlement of criminal cases by involving the perpetrator, victim, family of the perpetrator/victim, and other related parties to jointly seek a fair settlement by emphasizing restoration to the original state, and not retaliation.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency. 32.

Article 20

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency. 32.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency. 32.

The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government (1) as referred to in Article 17 letter a, include:

d. allocating budget for the protection of women and children from acts of violence according to regional financial capacity.

3. The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions.
4. Further provisions regarding the regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be further stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 30

2. Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to fully explain the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is the Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children in the working area of several Sub-districts at the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bengkalis Regency. 33. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for criminal acts of human trafficking. 34. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Sub-district and Village/Sub-village level. 35. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material/immaterial benefits. 36. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 37. Empowerment is a process of developing independence and welfare of a person or community by increasing knowledge and skills to meet their life needs both economically and socially. 38. Restorative Justice is the settlement of criminal cases by involving the perpetrator, victim, family of the perpetrator/victim, and other related parties to jointly seek a fair settlement by emphasizing restoration to the original state, and not retaliation.

Article 19

1. Parents, guardians and/or family legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
2. Parents and/or family must carry out prevention of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and prevailing norms.
3. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on court determination. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 12. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of Means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. 13. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19. Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bengkalis Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified standards. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency. 32.
